claims.statement: `modules/batches/data/batches.ts` is the repository's reference data contract (RULES.md rule 17) and is structured as three separated layers: a typed, `cache()`-wrapped fetch, the exported pure `mapBatchRow`, and derivation from the single `current_stage` enum; a `tenant_id` filter from a validated scope only selects the school because RLS remains the authorization boundary (rule 2).

The mapper preserves a null-means-not-recorded distinction for the billing deadline and turns every absent or unparseable date into the `Infinity` sentinel rather than `NaN`, because the sentinel is what downstream urgency tiering and countability checks treat as "no deadline".

Progress is derived as a count of distinct attended dates divided by the batch's snapshotted `total_sessions`, and both halves must exist for a value: an empty attendance embed is read as "unavailable" rather than as zero sessions held, and no `sessions_held` column exists so the figure cannot drift from the attendance it summarises.

The UI lifecycle pipeline is derived from the single `current_stage` enum through the total `DB_TO_UI_STAGE` map, where a new DB enum variant fails compilation until its UI treatment is chosen and both `completed` and `blocked` map to `null` so one marks everything done and the other marks nothing active.

Two lossy normalizations are paired with a preserved fact: the DB `blocked` status surfaces as UI `pending` while `Batch.blocked` is set from either `status` or `current_stage` for the attention queue, and the RQM code becomes `null` when blank while `Batch.id` stays the internal batch code so keys, URLs and lookups never follow the official code.

A batch's RQM code is unique per tenant via the partial unique index `batches_tenant_rqm_code_key`, so one RQM code means one batch and a colliding write is reported as `duplicate` rather than as a raw Postgres error.

`domain/rqm.ts` normalizes an RQM code before judging it — upper-casing, folding Unicode dashes to `-`, dropping invisibles and whitespace — gives a four-part NTP request number its own rejection message, and treats program or provider mismatches as warnings with provider numbers compared after stripping leading zeros.

The RQM Server Action resolves the tenant server-side from the URL tenant code against the caller's memberships and the role from `profiles.role` via `resolveTrustedRole`, then validates in `domain/`, writes in `data/`, appends activity, revalidates the tenant layout, and returns a discriminated `RqmFormState` instead of throwing.

The write only lands if the stored RQM code still equals `expectedPrevious` (`is('rqm_code', null)` for a null expectation), and a result matching zero rows is reported as `conflict-or-denied` because RLS refusal and a concurrent edit are indistinguishable through PostgREST.

Urgency is a pure tiering of precomputed days-to-billing with inclusive boundaries (negative `overdue`, ≤6 `critical`, ≤21 `warning`, else `on-track`), and a non-finite value reads as `muted` so the no-deadline sentinel is never styled as a deadline.

An open billing obligation is deliberately deadline-agnostic — not completed, billing report not verified, billing stage not done — and a separate predicate decides whether a recorded deadline makes it countable, so an undated obligation is surfaced as a data gap instead of being counted down.

The needs-attention queue is built from recorded facts only: a sync failure sorts first, urgent items precede due ones, an untracked document is not treated as missing, and all open batches without a recorded deadline collapse into one aggregate `billing-deadline-missing` row instead of one row per batch.
`NeedsAttentionQueue` renders at most eight items, states the remainder, conveys severity as a word plus an icon rather than colour alone, and hangs its empty copy off only what was actually checked.

`deriveDashboardMetrics` computes the one canonical KPI summary over a single active-batch population, leaves session progress `null` when no active batch has attendance, and reads no clock because every date figure is an already-computed `daysToBilling`.

`deriveTrainerMetrics` strips the billing figures from the summary object itself rather than only from its type, so the keys cannot serialize to a trainer screen, and `TrainerDashboardMetrics` omits them at compile time.

The trainer surface is trimmed server-side at the KPI layer rather than by CSS: the trainer dashboard fetches unfiltered batches, derives trainer metrics, and renders through a shell wrapper that passes no billing prop, so `KpiSummary`'s billing card has nothing to read.
Because the mapper is role-blind, the trainer trim relies on RLS for which batch rows and embedded document rows a trainer receives; rule 5's omission is only satisfied by the KPI and metric layers.

`domain/overview.ts` groups cross-school figures per school with the same metrics and attention functions the school dashboard uses, keeps schools with no batches present, orders schools by urgent count then open items then name, and exposes only urgent items as school-labelled cross-school exceptions.

`domain/alerts.ts` is a second reader of the same batch rows for the analytics alerts donut, and its `billing-ready` row uses the threshold-only `isBillingReady` signal so its copy must not claim the batch is ready to bill.

The dashboard route orders its guard ladder as forced denial, then `sync-failed` with zero rows before empty (rule 19), then no-tenant-access, then empty, and only renders the KPI row and queue when data exists; only admin and coordinator roles receive the RQM edit prop.

`tests/unit/batches.test.ts` freezes the clock with `vi.setSystemTime` around the days-to-billing block because that is the only mapper branch reading `Date.now()`, while `dashboard-domain.test.ts` needs no clock at all because `daysToBilling` arrives precomputed.
`billing_deadline` has no edit or import path anywhere in the UI and can only arrive with the row, whereas `rqm_code` is editable from the card and table views by admin and coordinator roles.
`Batch.ntpLag` has no source in the mapper, so the `ntp-lag` alert category can never fire and a test pins that the field never claims a lag.
